standard.name: Random-design density bounded above and below

novel.justification: This condition represents a designed-depletion or calibrated loss-to-follow-up regime, rather than ordinary administrative censoring with an atom at the horizon. Concretely, let the observed censoring time be the earlier of two conditionally independent continuous loss or availability times whose conditional survivals each vanish linearly as \(t\uparrow1\); their product has the known quadratic endpoint order, while smooth treatment- and covariate-dependent deviations are absorbed into the unknown residual \(g_a\). The design or external follow-up protocol supplies only the endpoint order \(2\), not the censoring law or \(g_a\), so nuisance learning remains necessary.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal P_4\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_4:=\{P:P\text{ satisfies consistency, conditional exchangeability, conditional independent censoring, the displayed density and treatment-overlap bands, the event-hazard band, the exact quadratic censoring factorization with its residual envelope and survival shape, and the three radius-}20\text{ Hölder conditions for every }a\in\{0,1\}\}\).

definitions.name: integrated orthogonal score \(\psi_a\)
definitions.construction: \[\psi_a(\bar\eta;O):=\bar m_a(X)-\frac{\mathbf 1\{A=a\}}{\bar\pi_a(X)}\left\{\frac{\Delta\bar H_a(U,X)}{\bar G_a(U\mid X)}-\int_0^U\frac{\bar H_a(t,X)\bar\lambda_a(t,X)}{\bar G_a(t\mid X)}\,dt\right\}.\]

definitions.name: quadratic-endpoint local-cubic learning handle
definitions.construction: On each training fold of size \(M\), use a deterministic \(h_M\)-partition of \([0,1]^2\), normalized monomials of total degree at most three, at-risk weighted local Nelson--Aalen equations for \(\lambda_a\), and direct weighted local equations for \(q_a=S_ag_a\); recover \(g_a\) by division by the survival generated from the hazard fit, clip all primitive fits to their known bands, and use deterministic in-band fallbacks whenever a random Gram eigenvalue is below its class-known population-scale threshold.

definitions.name: total cross-fitted estimator and variance estimator
definitions.construction: Split the indices deterministically into two folds, learn \(\widehat\eta_{-k(i)}\) by def:endpoint-learning-handle on the opposite fold, set \(W_i:=\psi_1(\widehat\eta_{-k(i)};O_i)-\psi_0(\widehat\eta_{-k(i)};O_i)\), and define \(\widehat\theta:=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nW_i\) and \(\widehat V:=\max\{n^{-1},n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(W_i-\widehat\theta)^2\}\); use the fixed values \(0\) and \(1\) for \(\widehat\theta\) and \(\widehat V\), respectively, when \(n<4\) or the observed sample lies outside its declared support.

definitions.name: quadratic-endpoint heavy-tail witness \(P^{\star}\)
definitions.construction: Under \(P^{\star}\), let \(X\sim\mathrm{Unif}[0,1]\), \(\pi_1(x)=0.4+0.2x\), \(\lambda_a(t,x)=1+a/2+x/4\), and \(g_a(t,x)=\exp(-xt/4)\); generate conditionally independent potential event times with these hazards and censoring times with survival \((1-t)^2g_a(t,x)\), and set the observed variables by consistency.

statements.statement: For the total data maps \((\widehat\theta,\widehat V)\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_4}P\!\left(\left|\sqrt n(\widehat\theta-\theta)-n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nD(O_i)\right|>\varepsilon\right)\to0,\qquad \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_4}P\!\left(\left|\widehat V/V_P-1\right|>\varepsilon\right)\to0,\] and \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_4}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}\left|P\!\left(\frac{\sqrt n(\widehat\theta-\theta)}{\sqrt{\widehat V}}\le z\right)-\Phi(z)\right|\to0.\] The construction uses only \((O_i)_{i=1}^n\) and the known constants defining \(\mathcal P_4\).
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: feasible efficient inference at the fixed horizon despite quadratic loss of follow-up and entirely learned nuisances.
statements.gap: Westling et al. (2024) obtain RMST inference by integrating a survival-curve limit under a censoring floor and assumed nuisance product rates; Tian et al. (2020) treat an unadjusted Kaplan--Meier integral without learned conditional causal nuisances.
statements.consumer: It supplies a fixed-horizon adjusted RMST confidence interval for the parotid-carcinoma analysis and a theoretically justified endpoint mode for CFsurvival.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_4^{\circ}\), \(D=D_1-D_0\) is the observed-data canonical gradient of \(\theta\) in the locally unrestricted independent-censoring model, the tangent closure generated by admissible smooth submodels has squared norm \(V_P\), and every regular estimator has asymptotic variance at least \(V_P\); the estimator in thm:uniform-endpoint-efficiency attains this bound.
statements.justification: A Gaussian limit alone is insufficient; this result certifies that the singular endpoint score is the efficiency benchmark and that the feasible procedure attains it.
statements.gap: Westling et al. (2024), Theorem 2, derives the survival-at-time gradient under positive censoring through the horizon, while the present gradient is the directly integrated fixed-endpoint score on a model with \(G_a(1\mid x)=0\).
statements.consumer: The efficiency certificate lets applied analysts compare alternative adjusted RMST procedures on the correct endpoint information scale.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_4\) and every deterministic triple \(\bar\eta\) satisfying the primitive bands, \[E_P[\psi_a(\bar\eta;O)]-\theta_a=E_P\!\left[\int_0^1S_a(t\mid X)\bar H_a(t,X)\left\{\frac{\pi_a(X)g_a(t,X)}{\bar\pi_a(X)\bar g_a(t,X)}-1\right\}\{\bar\lambda_a(t,X)-\lambda_a(t,X)\}\,dt\right].\] In particular, its absolute value is bounded by a class constant times \(\lVert\bar\lambda_a-\lambda_a\rVert_\infty(\lVert\bar g_a-g_a\rVert_\infty+\lVert\bar\pi_a-\pi_a\rVert_\infty)\).
statements.justification: The identity removes the apparent endpoint singularity before bounding the nuisance remainder and exposes the exact orthogonal product drift.
statements.gap: Westling et al. (2024), Supplementary Lemma 1 and the proof of Theorem 4, give the survival-curve drift; direct time integration and cancellation of the known quadratic factor are not developed there.
statements.consumer: It converts primitive uniform local-polynomial rates into the second-order remainder required by the fixed-endpoint estimator.

statements.statement: There exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that \(c\le V_P\le C\) for every \(P\in\mathcal P_4\), and for every fixed \(p\in(2,3)\), \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_4}E_P|D(O)|^p<\infty.\] One admissible envelope is a class constant times \(1+\Delta/(1-U)+\log\{1/(1-U)\}\).
statements.justification: Uniform Studentization must be justified with more than two moments but without the false third- or fourth-moment shortcut.
statements.gap: Jing, Shao, and Wang (2003) treat self-normalized independent sums under finite \(2+\delta\) moments, while Westling et al. (2024) use bounded influence functions supplied by censoring positivity.
statements.consumer: This envelope supports ratio-consistent empirical influence variance and uniform Gaussian approximation for the feasible cross-fitted statistic.

statements.statement: Can the local-cubic handle in def:endpoint-learning-handle be completed as a measurable total learner such that, for class constants \(C,c>0\) and every sufficiently large training size \(M\), \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_4}P\!\left(\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\lVert\widehat\lambda_a-\lambda_a\rVert_\infty+\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\lVert\widehat g_a-g_a\rVert_\infty+\lVert\widehat\pi_1-\pi_1\rVert_\infty>Cr_M\right)\le CM^{-2}+CJ_M^2e^{-cMh_M^3},\] including simultaneous random-Gram inversion, fourth-order Taylor residuals, martingale numerator noise, random denominators, and fallbacks under every measurable \(f\) satisfying the density band?
statements.justification: This simultaneous last-cell concentration result is the genuine open construction on which primitive-class endpoint efficiency rests.
statements.gap: Cattaneo et al. (2024) have nondegenerate i.i.d. local information and a smooth design density; Jiang and Doksum (2003) stop below the upper support boundary; Munch et al. (2024) give integrated hazard rates under positive endpoint follow-up.
statements.consumer: A positive answer discharges every high-level nuisance-rate assumption in thm:uniform-endpoint-efficiency and is reusable for other censoring-depleted conditional functionals.

statements.statement: The constructed law \(P^{\star}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_4^{\circ}\), and at \(P=P^{\star}\) it satisfies \(E_P|D(O)|^{5/2}<\infty\) and \(E_P|D(O)|^3=\infty\).
statements.justification: The witness shows that the weak-moment argument is structural rather than cosmetic and rules out proofs that silently invoke a third moment.
statements.gap: The positive-censoring frameworks of Westling et al. (2024) and Díaz et al. (2019) exclude this endpoint behavior by construction.
statements.consumer: It gives referees and software authors a concrete stress test for variance and Studentization implementations.

statements.justification: The operational deliverable is an honest fixed-horizon confidence interval, not merely an oracle linear representation.
statements.gap: Existing causal RMST Wald procedures require positive follow-up or high-level nuisance conditions and do not establish uniform coverage on the displayed quadratic-endpoint primitive class.
statements.consumer: The result directly supports nominal confidence reporting for adjusted five-year RMST contrasts in CFsurvival-style analyses.

sampling_model.design: Two-fold cross-fitting under i.i.d. sampling from \(P\in\mathcal P_4\).
sampling_model.overlap: Censoring follow-up satisfies \(G_a(t\mid x)=(1-t)^2g_a(t,x)\) and vanishes at the fixed horizon.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Treatment propensity, event hazard, and rescaled censoring residual are unknown and learned foldwise by the endpoint local-cubic handle; no estimator-side rate is assumed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4 gives a cross-fitted asymptotic-linear survival estimator under a uniform censoring floor and high-level nuisance product rates, and Section 5.3 obtains RMST inference by integration.
Theorem A1 gives a Gaussian limit for an unadjusted Kaplan--Meier RMST integral at the support endpoint under a finite weighted tail integral.
The paper develops efficient covariate-adjusted RMST estimation for randomized trials at an ordinary fixed follow-up horizon.
Theorem 1 gives whole-support local-polynomial conditional-density rates under nondegenerate local information and a smooth positive design density.
Theorem 3.2 gives pointwise asymptotic normality for local-polynomial Nelson--Aalen hazard smoothing strictly below the upper support boundary.
Self-normalized Gaussian approximation for independent sums is available under finite \(2+\delta\) moments.

tldr: In a designed-depletion or calibrated loss-to-follow-up regime, the censoring time is the earlier of two conditionally independent continuous loss or availability times whose near-horizon survivals vanish linearly, giving the known quadratic endpoint order while leaving the smooth residual censoring law unknown. At the scientific horizon, this quadratic censoring makes the influence function for survival itself non-square-integrable, but the remaining-life factor in fixed-endpoint RMST cancels one endpoint power and leaves a finite efficiency bound. The proposal asks whether a total cross-fitted one-step estimator can attain that bound uniformly over the stated radius-20 Hölder primitive class while learning the treatment propensity, event hazard, and rescaled censoring residual. Its open mathematical core is simultaneous local-cubic concentration in the last time--covariate cells, where only \(Mh_M^4\) information remains. The resulting nuisance rate \((\log n/n)^{1/3}\), exact product drift, weak \(5/2\)-moment Studentization, canonical-gradient certificate, and uniform Wald coverage together form the publishable kernel.

project_justification.gap: Westling et al. establish machine-learning inference for treatment-specific survival and integrated RMST under a censoring floor and high-level nuisance-rate conditions. Classical endpoint Kaplan--Meier theory permits vanishing follow-up for integrated functionals but has no conditional confounding adjustment or learned nuisance blocks. Existing local-polynomial hazard theory does not supply uniform last-cell concentration when the predictable risk set collapses quadratically.
project_justification.niche: The nonempty niche is a fixed-target efficiency theorem on a primitive smooth class where survival-at-endpoint inference is irregular, RMST remains regular, the nuisance fits must preserve the known quadratic factor, and the feasible score may lack a third moment.
project_justification.fill: The project integrates the survival score before analysis, learns the smooth event hazard and \(q_a=S_ag_a\) by boundary-adaptive cubic risk-set equations, derives their terminal-cell rate without assuming it, propagates the exact product drift through cross-fitting, and proves variance consistency and a uniform Studentized limit from a \(5/2\)-moment envelope.

related_work: Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024) is the writing and estimation exemplar: its Introduction moves from confounding and dependent censoring to a cross-fitted doubly robust survival estimator; Theorem 4 and Supplementary Lemmas 1--3 supply the foldwise decomposition and exact drift that are adapted here. Its condition B2 requires censoring survival bounded away from zero through the horizon, and Section 5.3 derives RMST inference by integrating the resulting survival-process limit. Tian et al. (2020), Theorem A1, and Stute (1995) show that an integrated Kaplan--Meier target can retain a Gaussian endpoint limit under a weighted tail integral; they neither adjust for covariates nor estimate conditional causal nuisances. Díaz et al. (2019) establish efficient covariate-adjusted RMST estimation in randomized trials with ordinary follow-up. Cattaneo et al. (2024), Theorem 1 and Appendix A.5, provide normalized local-polynomial bases, boundary-uniform Gram control, and Bernstein covering arguments under nondegenerate i.i.d. information. Jiang and Doksum (2003), equations (2.5)--(2.8) and Theorems 3.2 and 3.4, provide the Nelson--Aalen local-polynomial algebra but restrict asymptotics below an upper boundary with positive risk. Fan and Guerre (2016) provide whole-support polynomial reproduction and boundary matrix geometry, although their smooth design-density condition must be replaced by a direct density-band sandwich. Munch et al. (2024), Theorem 9 and Corollary 13, give integrated conditional-hazard rates for highly adaptive lasso under positive endpoint follow-up. Efromovich (2024) gives sharp mean-integrated-squared-error theory for conditional hazard estimation under right censoring, not simultaneous endpoint sup-norm control. Jing, Shao, and Wang (2003) supply the weak-moment self-normalization template, while Chernozhukov et al. (2018) supply foldwise conditioning and orthogonal product-remainder organization. Searches through September 11, 2026 found no result combining fixed-endpoint causal RMST efficiency, quadratic conditional follow-up loss, primitive learned-nuisance rates, and uniform feasible Studentization.
technical_internal_limitation: The decisive kill test is the terminal-cell version of oeq:primitive-endpoint-concentration. The population at-risk Gram has order \(Mh_M^4\), while a single contribution can be of order \(h_M\); the proof must preserve coercivity under an arbitrary measurable density \(f\), control the martingale numerator and Taylor remainder simultaneously, and make every low-count fallback uniformly negligible. If an omitted term forces error of order \(n^{-1/4}\) or worse, the main theorem cannot be obtained from the current handle. Numerical values from the presolve witness are diagnostics and are not theorem claims.
honest_scope: Identification of the fixed contrast is standard; estimation and inference at the quadratic endpoint are open. The theorem fixes the horizon \(1\), censoring exponent \(2\), one-dimensional covariate, smoothness order \(4\), and all radius and band constants. It does not cover an estimated endpoint exponent, a shorter moving horizon, a parametric hazard subclass, or a different target. As an in-class sanity check, fix \(\delta\in(0,1)\), set \(\tau:=1-\delta\), and diagnostically restrict the same factor-preserving learner and score integrals to \([0,\tau]\). Every \(P\in\mathcal P_4\) then obeys \(G_a(t\mid x)\ge\delta^2/2\) on \([0,\tau]\), so the construction is compared in the ordinary positive-follow-up regime covered by Westling et al. (2024), while retaining its factor-preserving algebra. This diagnostic restriction is only a sanity check and does not change the fixed horizon-\(1\) target or introduce a censoring-floor assumption into the main result. The general censoring-exponent phase diagram remains a separate flagship question.

seed_details.anchor: westling2024inference, Introduction, Theorems 2 and 4, Section 5.3, Supplementary Lemmas 1--3, proof of Theorem 4, and Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Construct a total learned-nuisance estimator attaining the canonical-gradient bound uniformly at a fixed horizon where conditional censoring survival vanishes quadratically.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Integrate the survival score before applying the replacement bound, so that the remaining-life weight cancels one endpoint power, and replace condition B2 by weighted local concentration.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for fixed-endpoint causal RMST, vanishing conditional censoring, semiparametric efficiency, and learned Hölder nuisances found no occupied target--method pair.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Westling et al. because Section 5.3 integrates their survival influence function.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their RMST argument inherits a survival-process theorem whose condition B2 imposes a censoring floor; the endpoint score replacement and bounded-score CLT both fail when \(G_a(1\mid x)=0\).
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The rate hypotheses are derived from the primitive class, the endpoint remains fixed, and the construction is neither a known-nuisance nor a parametric analogue.

seed_details.anchor: stute1995clt, main integrability theorem and proof; yang1994kmclt, martingale tail condition; westling2024inference, Theorems 2 and 4
seed_details.opportunity: Derive the if-and-only-if regularity and attainable-rate phase diagram when \(G_a(t\mid x)=(1-t)^\beta g_a(t,x)\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the fixed tail integral by a \(\beta\)-indexed tangent norm, then match its divergence threshold with endpoint-local least-favorable hazard perturbations and feasible nuisance rates.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for polynomial censoring exponents, causal RMST pathwise differentiability, and minimax endpoint hazard learning found classical unadjusted integrability conditions but no adjusted phase diagram.
seed_details.red_team: The threshold \(\beta<3\) follows immediately by power counting the oracle influence variance.
seed_details.rebuttal: Power counting gives only oracle square integrability; necessity in the causal tangent model, smoothness-dependent attainable regions, and a matching feasible or impossible procedure require distinct arguments.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed includes both regular and irregular directions and does not equate a finite oracle variance with feasible uniform estimation.

seed_details.anchor: cattaneo2024boundary, Introduction, Theorem 1, Appendix A.5, and Conclusion; jiangdoksum2003local, equations (2.5)--(2.8), Theorems 3.2 and 3.4, and proof
seed_details.opportunity: Prove simultaneous \((\log n/n)^{1/3}\) sup-norm rates for conditional hazard and rescaled risk fits when the last cell has only \(nh^4\) information and the covariate density is merely banded.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the nondegenerate i.i.d. Gram by an at-risk predictable Gram normalized at \(nh^4\), and replace ordinary numerator Bernstein by martingale concentration with total fallbacks.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for vanishing-risk local-polynomial hazards and endpoint-uniform conditional hazards found only interior, positive-risk, or integrated-loss results.
seed_details.red_team: This is the ordinary two-dimensional local-polynomial rate after changing the effective sample size.
seed_details.rebuttal: The random risk-set Gram, single-jump martingale numerator, endpoint Taylor geometry, and arbitrary measurable design density invalidate the ordinary regression concentration proof.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The claim names the estimator class, the terminal information scale, the uniform norm, and the first proof step that changes.

seed_details.anchor: jingShaoWang2003selfnormalized, main self-normalized deviation theorem and truncation proof; westling2024inference, Theorem 4 and variance construction
seed_details.opportunity: Transfer finite-\(5/2\)-moment self-normalization from oracle independent sums to fold-dependent estimated RMST scores and prove uniform variance consistency.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Condition foldwise, truncate the oracle score at a deterministic level, and prove the estimated-score replacement is negligible in the empirical second moment under the common endpoint envelope.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for cross-fitted self-normalization with endpoint-singular survival scores found generic DML moment conditions but no quadratic-censoring result.
seed_details.red_team: An ordinary Slutsky argument with the empirical influence variance already proves the result.
seed_details.rebuttal: The feasible scores share training folds, may have infinite third moments, and contain random endpoint denominators; uniform replacement and a truncated law of large numbers must be established.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The limit law is the focal object and is derived from a primitive weak-moment envelope rather than assumed.

seed_details.anchor: westling2024inference, Theorem 4 and Section 5.3; stute1995clt, optimal tail-integrability condition
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize the censoring-exponent frontier on which curve-first integration and directly integrated one-step RMST inference agree or diverge.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Compute separate tangent norms for endpoint survival and its time integral before comparing empirical replacement remainders.
seed_details.destination_search: No paper located states an observed-primitive divergence frontier between these two named estimation routes under polynomial conditional censoring.
seed_details.red_team: The difference is only that integration smooths the score.
seed_details.rebuttal: A publishable result would derive an observable exponent--smoothness frontier and prove both equivalence and strict divergence, not merely assert smoothing.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed was not selected because the exponent phase diagram is broader and less feasible than the fixed-quadratic theorem.

seed_details.anchor: westling2024inference, identification and cross-fitted survival score; diaz2019improved, efficient adjusted RMST construction
seed_details.opportunity: Learn a treatment rule maximizing fixed-endpoint RMST and derive regret under quadratic censoring as a function of policy complexity and endpoint nuisance rates.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a fixed RMST contrast by a policy-indexed orthogonal score and establish a uniform modulus over the policy class under the singular endpoint envelope.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for RMST policy learning under vanishing censoring found treatment-rule work under ordinary overlap but no quadratic-endpoint regret theorem.
seed_details.red_team: This follows from generic doubly robust policy learning after substituting an RMST score.
seed_details.rebuttal: Generic regret bounds assume bounded or well-behaved scores; the endpoint score has only sub-third moments and its nuisance remainder is weighted by collapsing follow-up.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The decision rule and regret, rather than estimation error for a fixed contrast, are the named objects.

seed_details.anchor: westling2024inference, censoring positivity condition B2; tian2020endpoint, Theorem A1 and Discussion
seed_details.opportunity: Quantify sensitivity of endpoint RMST inference to a local error in the known quadratic censoring factor and derive a critical misspecification radius for Wald sign reversal.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Insert a multiplicative tail perturbation into the integrated drift and solve for the least perturbation that moves the Studentized interval across zero.
seed_details.destination_search: No critical-tail-misspecification analysis for fixed-endpoint causal RMST was found, although generic positivity sensitivity work exists.
seed_details.red_team: The critical radius is merely the reported estimate divided by a derivative.
seed_details.rebuttal: The derivative is an endpoint-weighted functional with learned censoring and hazard components, and a valid result requires uniform remainder and identified sensitivity bounds.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed has a named critical radius but was not selected because the topic fixes the exponent as known rather than uncertain.

seed_details.anchor: tian2020endpoint, Introduction, Theorem A1, Discussion, and endpoint extrapolation paragraph; stute1995clt, endpoint CLT
seed_details.opportunity: Derive a joint limit law for covariate-adjusted RMST when the reporting horizon is selected from the observed follow-up distribution under conditional quadratic depletion.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Tian et al.'s marginal maximum-follow-up expansion by a conditional, cross-fitted horizon derivative coupled to the integrated causal score.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found random-horizon unadjusted RMST and fixed-horizon adjusted RMST, but not their endpoint-depleted combination.
seed_details.red_team: Apply the delta method jointly to a horizon estimator and the RMST estimator.
seed_details.rebuttal: At the support endpoint the horizon has an extreme-value rather than ordinary smooth limit, and its interaction with learned conditional weights is not a standard delta-method calculation.

seed_details.anchor: westling2024inference, observational identification setup and Section 5 inference
seed_details.opportunity: Seek finite-sample confidence sets for the fixed-endpoint RMST contrast by inverting a symmetry-based counterfactual score.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Identify an exact observable group action preserving the censored observational law while varying the counterfactual contrast.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for conformal or permutation RMST inference under observational confounding and right censoring found no exact symmetry compatible with the required nuisance learning.
seed_details.red_team: Conditional exchangeability is sufficient to permute treatment labels after propensity weighting.
seed_details.rebuttal: Weighting does not create finite-sample exchangeability when propensities and censoring laws are unknown; no exact group action is available under the primitive class.

literature_map.settled: Identification, the positive-follow-up efficient score, the cross-fitted fold decomposition, high-level product remainders, and unadjusted endpoint integrability are settled.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: No located paper proves fixed-endpoint causal RMST efficiency with quadratic conditional censoring, all three nuisance blocks learned from the displayed primitive Hölder class, and uniform feasible Studentization.
literature_map.closest_subsumption_check: Westling et al. require a censoring floor in B2; Tian et al. have neither conditional causal nuisances nor observational adjustment; Díaz et al. work in randomized trials with ordinary follow-up. None subsumes the kernel.
literature_map.exemplars_used: Westling et al. for the setup arc, score, exact drift, and cross-fitting; Stute and Tian et al. for endpoint integrability; Chernozhukov et al. for foldwise orthogonal replacement.

literature_map.settled: Boundary-adaptive local-polynomial bases, nondegenerate Gram concentration, pointwise Nelson--Aalen hazard smoothing, and integrated-loss conditional-hazard rates are settled.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: The targeted search found no simultaneous sup-norm theorem for a predictable risk-set Gram with \(nh^4\) terminal information under an arbitrary measurable band-bounded design density.
literature_map.closest_subsumption_check: Cattaneo et al. and Fan--Guerre assume nondegenerate local information and smoother design laws; Jiang--Doksum stop below the upper boundary; Munch and Efromovich use different loss and follow-up regimes.
literature_map.exemplars_used: Cattaneo et al. for normalized bases, Gram inversion, covering, and Bernstein control; Jiang--Doksum for hazard moment equations; Fan--Guerre for boundary polynomial geometry.

literature_map.settled: Self-normalized Gaussian approximation for exact independent sums with a finite \(2+\delta\) moment and cross-fitted orthogonal asymptotic linearity under regular scores are settled.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: No located result transfers weak-moment self-normalization to fold-dependent estimated survival scores with endpoint-diverging denominators and primitive uniform nuisance rates.
literature_map.closest_subsumption_check: Jing--Shao--Wang do not address estimated summands; Westling et al. avoid the issue with bounded scores; generic DML does not analyze a censoring-endpoint envelope.
literature_map.exemplars_used: Jing--Shao--Wang for truncation and self-normalized comparison, and Westling plus Chernozhukov et al. for the feasible-to-oracle foldwise transfer.

literature_checklist.author: Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone
literature_checklist.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 4 proves cross-fitted survival asymptotic linearity under B2 censoring positivity and B5 product rates; Section 5.3 integrates that result for RMST.

literature_checklist.author: Tian, Jin, Uno, Lu, Huang, Anderson, and Wei
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem A1 gives the unadjusted endpoint Kaplan--Meier RMST limit under a weighted tail integral.

literature_checklist.author: Stute
literature_checklist.one_line: The paper characterizes central-limit behavior for Kaplan--Meier integrals through censoring-tail integrability.

literature_checklist.author: Díaz, Colantuoni, Hanley, and Rosenblum
literature_checklist.one_line: The paper develops efficient covariate-adjusted RMST estimators for randomized trials under ordinary fixed-horizon follow-up.

literature_checklist.author: Cattaneo, Chandak, Jansson, and Ma
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 1 and Appendix A.5 give boundary-uniform local-polynomial rates and Gram concentration with nondegenerate local information.

literature_checklist.author: Jiang and Doksum
literature_checklist.one_line: Equations (2.5)--(2.8) construct local-polynomial Nelson--Aalen hazard fits, and Theorems 3.2 and 3.4 establish pointwise and left-boundary limits below the upper support endpoint.

literature_checklist.author: Fan and Guerre
literature_checklist.one_line: The paper proves whole-support multivariate local-polynomial bias, boundary matrix geometry, and uniform linearization under smoother design conditions.

literature_checklist.author: Munch, Gerds, van der Laan, and Rytgaard
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 9 and Corollary 13 derive highly adaptive lasso conditional-hazard rates under bounded hazard and positive endpoint follow-up.

literature_checklist.author: Efromovich
literature_checklist.one_line: The paper gives sharp mean-integrated-squared-error theory for conditional hazard estimation under right censoring, not last-cell sup-norm control.

literature_checklist.author: Jing, Shao, and Wang
literature_checklist.one_line: The main self-normalized deviation theorem works under finite \(2+\delta\) moments for independent sums.
